a1_answer:
NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The proposed intervention is a duty-cycle modulation of the online water-wash system to introduce periodic high-velocity air purge cycles between washes. Standard practice uses a fixed water-wash schedule with no intervening gas-phase cleaning; this intervention introduces a new gas-phase cleaning mechanism that physically dislodges nascent deposits before they bond, using the existing compressor discharge air as the purge medium. The adjacent-technique clearance is conventional online water washing; the departure is the interposition of high-velocity gas purge cycles in the schedule, a duty-split not present in any standard gas turbine wash protocol. The mechanism attacks the failure's driving physics—deposit adhesion—by applying transient shear stress to blade surfaces during the critical early deposit formation window.

PHYSICS CHECK — The driving variable for fouling is the adhesion strength of nascent salt/hydrocarbon deposits, which increases with time and deposit thickness. The purge cycle imposes high-velocity gas flow (driving variable: shear stress τ) that applies a transient τ > τ_adhesion to the blade surface, mechanically dislodging deposits before they chemically bond. For a typical axial compressor with blade chord length 0.2 m and purge air velocity 80 m/s (achievable via existing discharge air), τ ≈ 0.5–1.0 kPa, exceeding the adhesion strength of fresh deposits (τ_adhesion < 0.2 kPa), reducing deposit accumulation by >50% per purge cycle based on fluid shear scaling laws.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — (all rows tagged per procurement rule)
- (a) Existing online water-wash system control logic
- (b) Standard programmable logic controller (PLC) timer module (commercial, 24 VDC, DIN-rail)
- (c) Duty-cycle schedule change: "Set PLC timer to execute purge cycle every 6 hours: 2 minutes at 100% compressor discharge air bleed (valve fully open), 578 minutes idle"

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Standard practice bill: (a) water-wash system, (b) wash fluid, (c) wash schedule (e.g., weekly). Intervention bill: (a) existing water-wash system, (b) PLC timer (same class as existing wash controller), (c) schedule change (no new hardware). Burden class: same (no installation cost, same maintenance, no consumable cost added). Operational loss: Purge cycles occur during compressor operation; no production curtailment (loss = 0).

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Install flow meter on discharge air bleed line; monitor compressor inlet delta-P and exhaust temperature continuously. Instruments: Existing pressure transducers, temperature sensors, and data acquisition system. Pass/fail: After 1000 operating hours with intervention, delta-P increase < 0.5% (vs. 5% in baseline) and heat rate recovery >=3%. Kill criterion: If delta-P exceeds baseline by >1% at any interval, test fails. Duration: 1000 hours (representative of overhaul interval).

ALLOWED_ROW_OUTSIDE: added measure 'Standard programmable logic controller' shares no allowed-list stem (no blade redesign or coating change; inlet filtration/coalescer and online water...)
PHYSICS_DIRECTION_UNSTATED: the answer must carry an explicit DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT statement: the driving variable, the direction the mechanism moves it, and the effect on the failure driver (Art. 25 direction-of-effect; the auditor judges whether the stated direction is correct)
UNPRICED_DUTY_CYCLE: the bill modulates a duty cycle or schedule but prices no operational cost (throughput/energy/availability, quantified or bounded) — the OPERATIONAL COST line is mandatory
MECHANISM_CLASS_UNSTATED: the bill does not declare 'MECHANISM CLASS: <one phrase>' — the diversity cap needs the declaration
